claims.text: In situ HRTEM with controlled heating can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at atomic resolution.
High-entropy stabilization may suppress significant morphological changes in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles up to approximately 700 °C.
High-entropy stabilization may suppress significant compositional changes in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles up to approximately 700 °C.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a uniform chemical distribution.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles can be synthesized using standard colloidal or physical-vapor methods.
Specialized TEM heating holders permit real-time, lattice-resolved imaging during heating.
Using a low electron dose rate minimizes electron-beam-induced effects.
Enhanced configurational entropy in five-metal nanoparticles lowers atomic mobility.
Lower atomic mobility delays phase segregation or coarsening in five-metal nanoparticles.
High mixing entropy reduces the chemical driving force for elemental clustering.
A reduced driving force for elemental clustering inhibits large-scale structural rearrangements during heating.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will exhibit only minor atomic rearrangements during heating to approximately 700 °C.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will have superior thermal stability relative to simpler alloy nanoparticles under the same conditions.
Monometallic or lower-entropy alloy nanoparticles typically undergo more pronounced reshaping, grain growth, or compositional segregation at comparable temperatures.
Beyond approximately 700 °C, the entropy benefit may be overcome and partial phase separation or coarsening may occur.
Local composition variations may alter the temperature at which phase separation or coarsening begins.
The onset and extent of structural change depend on sample history, synthesis impurities, and electron-beam effects.
